<reason>B won a competitive debate by making the live choice easier: a continental authentication spine is extra power, not the clinic. A had a coherent weighing story—certain exclusion versus contingent abuse, mobility, unaccountable status-quo surveillance—but never showed why service delivery uniquely requires an AU lookup path rather than national IDs plus presented credentials. B’s governance clash was unanswered: purpose limits and logs do not create a hearing in states without courts, and service-tied “consent” is belonging, not choice. Function creep, weakest-link interoperability, and manufactured exclusion then outweighed A’s “feed first, fight later” sequencing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s collapse of A’s consent/governance story: when bread or care require the ID to talk, verification is coerced; an AU handshake still leaves no judge, so logs become a cleaner query path rather than redress.</best_rebuttal>
